Mean-log versus total-power proof and scoped supervised-objective proof
sources.details: For one band with two positive time powers, mean(log[1,9])=(ln1+ln9)/2=ln3 and mean(log[3,3])=ln3, while the power sums are10 and6. Therefore the mean-log summary does not identify total power. In general μ_j=(1/T)Σ_t ln(max(P_tj,1e-8)) is invariant under reindexing the same T terms, not a total of power or energy. For two equally weighted examples with opposite correct first-arrival labels0 and1, an identical predicted class0 probability p on both gives mean CE=−(lnp+ln(1−p))/2≥ln2, because p(1−p)≤1/4. Distinguishing the examples can reduce this direct supervised objective. This analytical inequality is a hand derivation; the finite logits below were separately executed. It does not prove that labels guarantee optimization, no shortcuts or generalization, and it is not a necessity theorem for all learning. wav2vec2.0’s masked-latent contrastive objective is another source of temporal representation learning; it is not a demonstrated first-arrival QA system.
